title: Client confidence fallback protocol notes
content:
Purpose:

A compact personal sketch for an end-to-end client-side confidence scoring + fallback protocol. The goal is to let SDKs and edge proxies make safe, deterministic fallback decisions when upstream LLM responses are low-confidence, high-latency, or fail quality checks — without round-tripping to control-plane every time.

High-level goals:
- allow clients to downgrade to cheaper/shorter/safer model variants automatically based on a local confidence signal
- keep decisions auditable (telemetry/event traces) and reversible (server can override via policy)
- minimize surface area: primitive shapes for confidence header, simple config, and a compact state machine for SDKs
- design for flaky networks and partial responses (stream truncation)

Non-goals:
- not an attempt to replace server-side robust evaluation or long-term quality regression monitoring
- not prescribing a specific ML confidence model (scalar from 0..1 is enough)

API / wire shapes (text examples):

1) Upstream response envelope (HTTP JSON body + headers):

headers:
  X-RW-Confidence: 0.27    # optional; preferred priority if present
  X-RW-Model-Variant: redwood-v2-medium
  X-RW-Response-Integrity: sha256:abcd...  # for audit and replay checks

body (JSON):
{
  "id": "resp_...",
  "output": "...generated text...",
  "meta": {
    "confidence_estimate": 0.27,
    "token_certainty_stats": {"avg": 0.55, "low_pct": 0.12},
    "quality_flags": ["hallucination:low", "formatting:ok"]
  },
  "truncated": false
}

Notes: header scalar is a fast-path; body.meta is ground truth for audits. Clients prefer header when both present to avoid parsing body in streaming scenarios.

2) Client config (local SDK settings) - small YAML-like shape:

confidence_fallback:
  enabled: true
  threshold: 0.4            # if confidence < threshold, consider fallback
  cooldown_seconds: 30      # after a fallback, suppress repeated fallbacks briefly
  preferred_fallbacks:      # ordered list of model variants or route tags
    - redwood-v1-small
    - redwood-v2-compact
  max_retries: 2            # attempts to recover by contacting upstream fallback route
  telemetry_level: minimal  # none|minimal|detailed
  server_override_ttl: 120   # server-provided override header will be honored for X seconds

3) Server-to-client policy header (optional):

X-RW-Fallback-Policy: fallback=redwood-v1-small;threshold=0.35;ttl=60

This lets the control-plane nudge clients without forcing an immediate block; clients only accept if server_override_ttl not expired.

Client state machine (plain text):
- IDLE: request sent, awaiting stream/body
- EVALUATE: on receiving confidence header/body, compute decision
    - if confidence >= effective_threshold => ACCEPT -> emit ACCEPT event, render response
    - else => attempt FALLBACK -> emit FALLBACK-ATTEMPT event
- FALLBACK-ATTEMPT: send new request to fallback variant (in preferred_fallbacks)
    - on success confidence >= threshold => FALLBACK-SUCCESS -> render
    - else try next fallback up to max_retries -> FALLBACK-FAIL -> emit FAIL and render primary response with warning
- COOLDOWN: after a FALLBACK-SUCCESS or FALLBACK-FAIL, suppress fallback attempts for cooldown_seconds

Edge cases:
- streaming response truncated mid-stream: mark as truncated=true; trigger EVALUATE once end-of-stream or first major checkpoint token arrives (heuristic: after punctuation or N tokens)
- missing confidence signals: consult local heuristics (e.g., token entropy proxy) then fall back to optimistic accept unless policy forces fallback
- high latency: if server announces extended tail latency (header X-RW-Est-Latency > client timeout), then proactively attempt cheaper fallback in parallel (hedged fallback).

Telemetry and events (minimal list):
- rw.client.confidence.event => {"phase":"EVALUATE","confidence":0.27,"route":"hosted:redwood-v2"}
- rw.client.fallback.attempt => {"to":"redwood-v1-small","reason":"low_confidence","retry":0}
- rw.client.fallback.result => {"result":"success|fail","duration_ms":120}
- rw.client.server_override_applied => {"policy":"...", "ttl_remaining":90}

All telemetry should be redact-safe and not include full payloads by default; detailed mode can include response hashes for later audit.

Deployment/rollout notes:
- start with telemetry_level:minimal to collect signals from 10% of traffic (client opt-in flag in SDK config)
- A/B profile test: measure UX drop/recovery and per-token cost delta when fallback enabled vs disabled for same queries
- gate server-provided policy header parsing behind a feature flag until trustable ruleset validated

Ascii architecture sketch (two-line diagram):

CLIENT-SDK [request]
  |-> UPSTREAM /redwood/v2 (fast, premium) -> response with X-RW-Confidence header
  |                             
  |                              
  |-> FALLBACK /redwood/v1-small (cheaper)  <- parallel hedged attempt option

Alternative: client consults control-plane only for policy updates; fallback decision remains local.

Security/abuse considerations:
- don't expose internal policy rules in plain text to untrusted clients in a way that leaks capacity strategy; prefer signed policy blobs (short TTL)
- server override header must be authenticated and integrity protected (existing response signing plan / X-RW-Response-Integrity)
- clients should rate-limit fallback attempts to prevent amplification against internal fallback pools

Open questions / TODOs:
- how expressive should the condition language be? (threshold only vs pattern match on quality_flags)
- should we allow delta-based fallbacks (ask for shorter max_tokens instead of different model)?
- UX for developers: surface clear signals in SDK (events + simplest boolean API) vs full config knobs
- add example unit tests for streaming truncation heuristics (we need deterministic fixtures)

Next steps (personal action items):
- prototype small JS SDK shim that implements state machine above (2d spike, 3 days)
- add telemetry stubs and send to local dev infra for 10% sample
- discuss server policy header signing format with security (assign to Samir)
- write a lightweight RFC for eng-serving-runtime to socialize (target weekly sync)

References and related tickets:
- CONFLUENCE-1298: "Fallback patterns & capacity planning"
- JIRA-847: "Telemetry schema: client fallback events"
- GH-PR-4521: "SDK header parsing improvements"

Notes to self: keep heuristics simple at first. Avoid combinatorial explosion in config. Track false positives (cases where fallback hurts quality) closely and expose an easy "opt-out" developer toggle.

---

End of sketch.
